codeReview.summary: Well-structured research output validator with clear separation between structural and content checks. The script is both importable as a module and runnable as a CLI, following the existing script conventions (shebang, JSDoc header, import.meta.main guard). All 8 validation criteria are implemented correctly: YAML frontmatter validation, required section checking (variant-aware), file:line reference counting, code block length enforcement, and 4 documentarian-mode content checks (prescriptive, evaluative, debugging, plan contamination). Test coverage is thorough with 84 tests across unit, fixture-based integration, and cross-variant scenarios. The 5 fixture files are well-crafted to exercise specific failure modes. The code properly handles edge cases like code block boundaries in pattern scanning and Open Questions section exclusion for content checks.

issues.description: Empty test body: 'also fails prescriptive language check (contains \'should\')' has no assertions — only comments explaining the fixture doesn't actually contain prescriptive language. The test passes vacuously. Should either add an assertion (e.g., expect prescriptive check to pass) or remove the misleading test name.

CLI output mixes human-readable colored output (lines 559-582) with raw JSON (line 586) on stdout. When used programmatically (piped), consumers would need to separate the formatted header from the JSON payload. Consider sending the human-readable portion to stderr and only JSON to stdout, or adding a --json flag to suppress the human-readable output.

The file:line ref regex could match URL-like patterns with ports (e.g., 'api.example.com:8080'). In practice this is unlikely in research output, but a stricter regex requiring a path separator before the filename would reduce false positives.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The validate-research command was added to .factory/services.yaml as 'validate-research: bun run scripts/validate-research-output.ts'. This was likely added by a prior or parallel feature, since services.yaml already includes this entry — no gap here.

Worker noted that the backend-worker skill's TDD procedure ('write tests first') is awkward when tests import the implementation module — writing tests first causes import failures. Worker suggested the skill should say 'create the module interface first, then tests, then fill in implementation'. This is valid feedback captured in skillFeedback.suggestedChanges.

summary: PASS. The research output validator and fixture test suite is well-implemented with comprehensive coverage. The validator correctly checks 8 quality criteria across both plan and standalone research variants. All 84 tests pass. Three non-blocking issues found: (1) one test has an empty body with a misleading name, (2) CLI mixes colored output with JSON on stdout which complicates programmatic consumption, (3) file:line ref regex has minor false positive potential with URL-like patterns. None of these block functionality.
